checks.name: V1 [sanity: isolated mu_2 reproduces the L232 parameter-free residual on the full sample] the isolated model rms is compared with L232's 0.1502 dex
checks.measured: isolated rms 0.1469 dex over 2296 points (120 galaxies)
checks.reading: the machinery reproduces the established parameter-free fit, so the EFE comparison below is trustworthy

checks.name: V2 [applying the EFE everywhere slightly WORSENS the full-sample fit, as expected: most SPARC galaxies are near-isolated] the EFE rms over ALL points is compared with the isolated rms
checks.measured: EFE rms 0.1957 vs isolated 0.1469 dex over the full sample
checks.reading: most galaxies sit in weak fields where the EFE should barely act, so forcing it everywhere cannot help globally. The test is not the global fit -- it is the OUTER points of the few galaxies that reach past r_x, done next

checks.name: V3 [does the EFE model fit the OUTER points better than isolated MOND?] the rms residual at points beyond r_x is compared between the two parameter-free models
checks.measured: 34 outer points in 10 galaxies: isolated rms 0.1354 dex, EFE rms 0.3043 dex (EFE better by -0.1689)
checks.reading: this is the confirmatory test. A lower EFE rms means the predicted downturn is actually present at the outer radii; a higher one means the EFE over-suppresses (as it did for dwarfs in L240) or is absent

checks.name: V4 [do the outer points show the predicted deficit -- obs BELOW isolated MOND?] the sign of log(gobs/g_isolated) at outer points is tested against the no-downturn null (half above, half below)
checks.measured: 14/34 outer points sit below isolated MOND (41%), median offset +0.0067 dex; sign-test p = 0.303
checks.reading: the EFE predicts outer points fall BELOW the flat-MOND expectation. A majority below with a negative median is the signature; a split near 50/50 means no detectable downturn at this footing and sample size

checks.name: V5 [the test is LOW POWER and is reported as a hint, not a result] the number of testable galaxies and the per-galaxy win rate are stated with their statistical limitation
checks.measured: only 10 galaxies reach past r_x; EFE fits better in 3/10; with 34 outer points a -0.1689 dex difference and sign-test p = 0.303 are HINT-level, not decisive
checks.reading: stated so the result cannot be over-read: SPARC simply does not contain many galaxies whose curves reach deep into their own EFE regime. A decisive test needs extended-HI curves (e.g. WHISP/Apertif) or a purpose-built deep-MOND-in-a-field sample, not this archive

checks.name: V6 [the negative is NOT a choice of EFE law, and it flips with the g_ext prescription -- so SPARC cannot settle it] the additive law is compared with the multiplicative, and the aggressive vs conservative external-field prescriptions are contrasted
checks.measured: additive law rms 0.2974 dex, essentially the same as multiplicative 0.3043 -- both over-predict the downturn vs isolated 0.1354; and with the conservative Newtonian-net g_ext the predicted breaks move OUTSIDE the data entirely (0 testable galaxies), consistent with the observed flatness
checks.reading: the failure is robust to the EFE law (both bracket and both over-suppress), and the whole test's existence depends on the approximation-dependent 2MRS field: the aggressive prescription predicts a downturn that is absent, the conservative one predicts almost no observable break at all (0 galaxies). SPARC cannot decide either way
